questions.q: What is a calculated field in Tableau?
options: A new field you define yourself with a formula, built from the fields already in your data source
A field that Tableau automatically creates from your database's primary key
A filter applied to an existing dimension
A saved chart type you can reuse across worksheets
questions.explain: A calculated field is a field you author with a formula in Tableau's calculation language — it doesn't exist in the raw data until you define it.

questions.q: How do you open the Calculation Editor to create a new calculated field?
options: Analysis > Create Calculated Field
File > New Field
Right-click the worksheet canvas > Insert Field
Format > Calculations
questions.explain: Analysis > Create Calculated Field opens the Calculation Editor dialog, where you name the field and write its formula.

questions.q: In the Data pane, how can you tell a field is calculated rather than coming directly from the data source?
options: It has an equals sign (=) next to its data-type icon
It's always colored red
It appears in a separate pane from all other fields
There's no visual difference — you have to remember which ones you made
questions.explain: Tableau marks every calculated field with a permanent equals sign (=) next to its data-type icon in the Data pane.

questions.q: What does the formula IIF([Sales] != 0, [Discount] / [Sales], 0) do?
options: Divides Discount by Sales when Sales isn't zero, and returns 0 otherwise, avoiding a divide-by-zero error
Always divides Discount by Sales, regardless of whether Sales is zero
Filters out every row where Sales equals zero
Sums Discount and Sales together
questions.explain: IIF(test, then_value, else_value) checks the test first — here, whether Sales isn't zero — before doing the division, which is exactly how the lesson's Discount Ratio formula avoids dividing by zero.

questions.q: What determines whether a new calculated field lands under Dimensions or Measures in the Data pane?
options: What the formula returns — a number becomes a Measure, text or a category becomes a Dimension
Alphabetical order of the field name
Whichever pane you clicked before opening the Calculation Editor
Calculated fields never appear under Measures, only Dimensions
questions.explain: Tableau decides Dimension vs. Measure based on the calculated field's return type — a numeric result (like Discount Ratio) becomes a Measure.
